action: Switch from Modify mode to Create mode.
Create a skeleton and leave the default joint names unchanged.
notes: The default names are used later in the IK Driven field.

action: Create a Pack Folder, connect the skeleton to it, and name the packed skeleton Base.
notes: The transcript refers to this as Base Scale; your notes identify the name as Base.

action: Set the Pack Folder type to Skeleton.
Create an Auto Rig Component and rename it IK.
notes: Connect the Pack Folder output to this component.

action: Select Smooth IK from the Component dropdown.
Open the Driven field and identify the joint names that the IK component must control.
notes: The example uses the default joint names 0, 0.1, and 0.2.

action: Add a marker to display joint names while working.
notes: Set Marker Text to use the name attribute and set the attribute to point.

action: Select the skeleton and enable the marker display to inspect the joint names.
notes: This makes the point names visible on the skeleton.

action: Enter the joint names into the IK Driven field and press Enter.
notes: Use the actual names displayed by the marker, such as 0, 0.1, and 0.2.

action: Check the IK result and identify that it is not working correctly yet.
notes: The IK component needs the FK transforms initialized first.

action: Create another Auto Rig Component before the IK component and rename it FK.
notes: Connect the FK component before IK in the rigging chain.

action: Select FK and set the transform, rotation, and scale promotion groups to *.
notes: The wildcard promotes all points' transform channels.

action: Test the FK controls, then return to the IK component and verify that IK now works.
notes: FK initializes the transforms required by IK.

action: Inspect the IK component's Controls section and identify the generated pole-vector and IK-handle control names.
notes: The example names are arm_pole_L and arm_ik_handle_L (the exact displayed spelling should be followed).

action: Remove the _L suffix from the pole-vector and IK-handle control names.
notes: Use center controls instead of left/right-specific controls.

action: Create a Configure Controls node and add two control configurations.
notes: Configure one entry for each generated IK control.

action: Set the first control group to the pole-vector control and the second to the IK-handle control.
notes: Use the updated names after removing _L.

action: Configure the appearance of both controls by adjusting their size, shape, and color.
notes: The example enlarges the controls, uses a blob shape, and assigns red to the IK control.

action: Create a Scene Add Character node and connect it after Configure Controls.
notes: Adds the character to the Apex evaluation scene.

action: Create a Scene Animate node and test the IK rig.
notes: The resulting arm IK rig should now be visible and usable.

action: Inspect the pole-vector control's initial position and identify that it is placed at the elbow.
notes: The IK component is using the middle joint, 0.1, as the initial pole-vector position.

action: Move the pole-vector control outward from the elbow to establish a better initial position.
notes: Position it away from the arm so the elbow points in the intended direction.

action: Test the IK handle by moving it and observe how the arm flips if the pole vector remains at the elbow.
notes: The elbow tries to point toward the pole vector, causing the arm to flip.

action: Introduce guides as the next method for defining initial rest positions for controls.
notes: This is an explanation of the next tutorial, not an operation performed here.
